fieldValues.title: Agent merge rights follow decision mode and door, the same in every governed repository
fieldValues.decision_question: When may an agent merge its own pull request, and does that rule differ between the repositories the programme governs?
fieldValues.context: srs states the rule in its CLAUDE.md 'Gates and choreography': a PR states its decision mode and door; an agent may label it gate:auto-merge only when the mode is clear or complicated AND the change is Door 1 (executes a recorded ruling) or non-normative (tooling, checks, docs); complex mode, Door 2 or Door 3 carries gate:owner-merge; chaotic stops. srs-rust consumes that rule by pointer. srs-web states no rule, so on 2026-10-23 a one-line .mcp.json change there (srs-web#608) had to wait for the owner while the identical change in srs and srs-rust merged itself. The owner asked to adopt the rule everywhere (2026-10-23).
fieldValues.friction: A repository without the rule sends every agent PR, however trivial, to the owner; each session rediscovers the gap and guesses which label to use.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
1. One rule everywhere (recommended): agent merge rights follow decision mode and door in every governed repository; the rule is stated once and each repository's CLAUDE.md points to it. Leads to: trivial, non-normative or already-ruled PRs stop queueing for the owner, while new meaning, user-visible behaviour, pins and format changes stay the owner's.
2. Owner-merge only where no rule is stated: repositories without the rule keep every agent PR for the owner. Leads to: maximum control there, and the owner's time spent on trivial PRs.
3. Do nothing: the gap stays unstated. Leads to: each session guesses, and labels differ between repositories for the same kind of change.
fieldValues.decision_statement: In every repository the programme governs, an agent may merge its own pull request only when the change's decision mode is clear or complicated and it either executes a recorded ruling (Door 1) or is non-normative (tooling, checks, docs); such a PR carries gate:auto-merge. Complex mode, a new ruling (Door 2) or an amendment to an accepted ruling's surface (Door 3), a change to user-visible behaviour, a pin advance or a format change carries gate:owner-merge, and the agent never merges it. Chaotic mode stops. The rule is stated once and each repository points to it rather than restating it.
fieldValues.rationale: One way over many: the same kind of change gets the same label everywhere, and a rule stated once cannot drift between copies. It keeps the owner's attention on the changes that carry meaning.
fieldValues.revisit_when: When an auto-merged change in any repository has to be reverted because it altered behaviour users rely on.
fieldValues.next_steps: Point srs-web's CLAUDE.md (and any governed repository without the rule) at the canonical statement; choose its single home (the srs CLAUDE.md section today, or the clerk handbook) and make every other copy a pointer.
